text: Theorem 6.1 (completeness) states that, for any class of functions on {0,1}^n, a distribution mu on inputs x, a language L in Gamma^O(n^c) with a recursive decomposition M_D of depth d and width q, 0 < gamma < 1/2 and a stability parameter rho, the protocol of Figure 2 run on M_D satisfies the following: if M_D is A-provable with probability 1-gamma over x drawn from mu, achieved by a function A* in the class, and is also rho-stable at x with respect to A* with probability 1-gamma, then there exists A in the class such that for all B (of any size), with probability at least 1-2gamma, E[V^{A,B}(x)] is at least 1/rho^(d+1).
title: Theorem 6.1 completeness: some A guarantees expected payoff at least 1/rho^(d+1) against every B
